title: Room, Equipment, and Supply Preparation

unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Prepare the examination or procedure room, equipment, and supplies for examinations and minor procedures.
- Maintain aseptic awareness, including hand hygiene, surface disinfection, and protection of sterile items.
- Check that the room, equipment, and supplies are ready before the provider arrives, and escalate or report problems rather than improvising.
- Apply standard precautions and bloodborne-pathogen safety when cleaning, stocking, and disposing of supplies and waste.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Before any guest arrives, you wipe down the table and counters so the room is clean and ready. That is the very first job, before turning on the computer or anything else.

### Question 2

Think of wiping a dirty plate before it goes in the dishwasher: you remove the food first so the soap can clean the plate. Cleaning first helps the germ-killer do its job.

### Question 3

High-touch surfaces are like the door knobs and railings everyone grabs with their hands, so those are the spots that need the most wiping between visitors.

### Question 4

It is like changing the paper cover and wiping the seat down between customers so no one catches the last person's germs.

### Question 5

It is like giving each new customer a fresh paper liner on a shared chair so they never sit where the last person sat.

### Question 6

A germ-killer needs time to work, like letting soap sit on your hands while you scrub. If you wipe it off too fast, it never finishes the job.

### Question 7

If the paper liner on a chair is ripped, you take it off and put on a new one instead of trying to cover the hole.

### Question 8

Even old, dried blood can carry germs, so you wear gloves and use the special cleaner, just like you would with fresh blood.

### Question 9

It is like closing the door and knocking before walking into someone's room so they are not surprised and their private space stays private.

### Question 10

If a guest room is too hot and a lamp is out, you fix or report it before the guest arrives, not after.

### Question 11

A cord across the floor is like a rope stretched across a doorway: you move it out of the way so no one trips.

### Question 12

A wet spot on the floor is like a spilled drink: you wipe it up or put a sign over it right away so no one slips on it.

### Question 13

A hand-washing station needs soap, towels to dry with, and hand sanitizer, like a bathroom sink fully stocked.

### Question 14

A sharps box is like a locked bin for sharp pencils: it stands up, stays near your desk, and never gets so full that things stick out.

### Question 15

When the sharp-items bin reaches the fill line, you seal it up and get a new one, because a too-full bin means sharp points can poke out.

### Question 16

Only things soaked with blood or body fluids go in the special red bin; everything clean goes in the normal trash.

### Question 17

Used sheets are like dirty laundry: you carry them gently to the hamper without shaking them, so dust and germs do not fly around.

### Question 18

If blood spills, you put on gloves, use the right cleaner, and throw the dirty wipes in the special red bin, not the kitchen sink.

### Question 19

You check the shelves in the morning like a store clerk stocking up before opening, so nothing is missing when customers arrive.

### Question 20

Expired supplies are like expired food: you throw them out and add them to the shopping list, you do not eat them.

### Question 21

It is like the grocery store putting the older milk in front so it gets used before it goes bad.

### Question 22

PPE is like safety gear kept near the workstation: gloves in every size, gowns, masks, and eye shields, all within reach.

### Question 23

Gloves are like shoes: they only protect well when they fit, so you keep several sizes available.

### Question 24

It is like laying out the bandages and tape before a small repair so everything is ready when it is needed.

### Question 25

Single-use packets are like tiny ketchup packets: each person gets a fresh one so no one shares germs.

### Question 26

If a sample might be taken, you get the right cup and the right label ready, just like putting a name tag on a jar before filling it.

### Question 27

If the cleaning wipes are dried out, you get a fresh container, because dry wipes can not clean anything.

### Question 28

Clean clothes go in the clean drawer, and dirty clothes go in the hamper; you never mix them.

### Question 29

There is a normal trash can and a special red bin for anything with blood on it, and they stay separate.

### Question 30

The doctor decides if the job needs super-clean (sterile) gloves or regular clean gloves, and the assistant follows those directions.

### Question 31

It is like checking that the flashlight works before handing it to someone who needs it.

### Question 32

If a tool is broken, you set it aside with a note and tell someone, instead of handing a broken tool to a customer.

### Question 33

You set up tools on the workbench near where they will be used, not in boxes in another room.

### Question 34

A scale is like a ruler that must start at zero, or the number you read will be wrong.

### Question 35

You clean a thermometer probe between people the same way you wash a spoon between uses.

### Question 36

It is like wiping down a shared tool before the next person uses it.

### Question 37

If a sealed snack bag is ripped and wet, you do not eat the snack; you throw it away and get a new one.

### Question 38

You check the seal and the date on a package, like checking that food is still sealed and not past its date.

### Question 39

Disposable things are like paper plates: you use them once and throw them away, not wash them for later.

### Question 40

The assistant makes sure the oxygen tank is there and that no one has a flame nearby, but a trained professional turns it on.

### Question 41

A fire extinguisher stays mounted and checked, not hidden in a closet, so it works when it is needed.

### Question 42

You check the vacuum works before cleaning a spill, not after you start.

### Question 43

You aim a desk lamp at the work, not in someone's eyes, and keep it from knocking anything over.

### Question 44

Tools that must be completely germ-free come sealed in their own clean package, like a fresh fork wrapped in its own napkin.

### Question 45

You get fresh, clean tablecloths and napkins ready for a special dinner, and you do not reuse yesterday's dirty ones.

### Question 46

Clean is washing your hands before dinner; sterile is the extra-clean setup used for surgery.

### Question 47

Once the clean zone is set up, only clean hands or gloves may touch it, like only clean hands touching the clean dishes.

### Question 48

It is like leaning over a freshly iced cake: bits from your sleeve can fall onto it.

### Question 49

If something dirty touches a clean item, you say something right away and get a clean one, even if no one saw it.

### Question 50

You wash your hands before and after helping each person, like a cook washing hands between handling different foods.

### Question 51

If your hands have actual dirt on them, wash with soap and water; hand sanitizer works for clean-looking hands.

### Question 52

After cleaning, let things dry on their own instead of blowing on them, so you do not add new germs.

### Question 53

If something might splash, you wear gloves, a mask, and goggles, like wearing goggles when something might splash in your eye.

### Question 54

You take off the dirtiest thing first, like removing muddy gloves before touching your clean clothes.

### Question 55

Gloves are like napkins: one use per person, then throw them away.

### Question 56

You never put the cap back on a used needle with your fingers, because that is how people get stuck.

### Question 57

You wipe the spots everyone touches, like the table and door handle, between each person.

### Question 58

A wet face mask is like a wet paper towel; you get a fresh dry one instead of keeping the soggy one.

### Question 59

Wash the dirt off first, then use the germ-killer, like scrubbing a pan before sanitizing it.

### Question 60

Aseptic awareness is like being careful with a freshly cleaned kitchen: keep clean things clean and do not put them where they can get dirty.

### Question 61

Before the guest arrives, you do a final look-around: clean, stocked, and everything working.

### Question 62

You make sure the customer's file is ready and complete before the meeting, not found later.

### Question 63

If a key ingredient is missing, you tell the cook right away and get the right one instead of throwing in something else.

### Question 64

If the right tool is missing, you tell the person in charge and only use a different tool if they approve it.

### Question 65

If you know what is being cooked, you set out the right tools and ingredients ahead of time.

### Question 66

If you do not know how to set something up, you ask for the instructions instead of guessing.

### Question 67

Between customers, you reset the table: wipe it down, fresh cover, and restock what was used.

### Question 68

Even if you are in a hurry, you still buckle your seatbelt; safety steps are never skipped.

### Question 69

If a tool breaks, you put a note on it and tell the manager, instead of hiding it or using it again.

### Question 70

Getting everything ready ahead of time is like setting the table before dinner, so the meal goes smoothly.

### Question 71

Standard precautions mean treating every patient the same safe way, because you cannot always tell who is carrying germs.

### Question 72

You unwrap clean items carefully and keep them clean, like not letting a sterile bandage touch a dirty table.

### Question 73

Clean supplies are not enough; you also need the germ-killer ready and used before the next person sits down.

### Question 74

You give the person a covering and close the door so they can change in private, the same way you would want.

### Question 75

You keep the spill kit in a known spot and know how to use it, just like knowing where the mop and bucket are.
